STEM courses for example have a pretty big workload, and usually take a while to complete (from my experience at least), and can cause some teens to be really busy and have limited free time to do what they want. Non-STEM courses are usually said to have a smaller and easier workload, which can definitely influence the amount of time a teen needs to study and complete their work. Secondly are other activities, for example extracurriculars, outside of school classes, tuition, or even plans to go somewhere/take a trip. This can also affect how busy a teen is during the day, if they are going somewhere then it can really reduce the amount of time they have to study and finish their work. Ever since the beginning of the Industrial Revolution, the world has been bombarded by human activities that have led to increased greenhouse gas emissions and pollution. The consequences of these activities have led to the ever increasing effects of climate change that impact both human and animal lives, therefore, it is important for us, humans, to reverse the effect before it is too late. 

Since the discovery of plastic, it has become a widely used resource for everyday accommodations such as in food packaging, water bottles, and others due to it being cheap to produce. However, plastic is not a renewable resource as it is made from fossil fuels and takes centuries if not more to decompose back into nature. Plastic waste is a huge problem in the modern world as most of it ends up in a landfill near water sources and animals. When these plastics break down into smaller particles called microplastics, they are ingested by animals and contaminate drinking water, which are then consumed by humans. The ingestion of microplastics has been linked with the increased risks of cancer as well as other health risks in humans.

The burning of fossil fuels for electricity is also a notorious practice by humans. As previously mentioned, fossil fuels are not renewable resources and when they are burned, greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide are released into the atmosphere. The increase of greenhouse gases feeds into an effect called the Greenhouse Effect, which is when light energy from the sun enters Earth but is then trapped as heat by the greenhouse gases. As a result of the increased greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere, there has been a trend of global warming that has been affecting the climate all over the world. These changes include more severe droughts, storms, and floods that endanger human livelihood in terms of both food production and shelter.   

Furthermore, the effects of climate change also pose a danger to the very basis of how the Earth works. Climate  change has generally been wiping out plants and animal species since its very beginning. Once it reaches a certain point where the relationships and symbiosis between different species are no longer able to work in cooperation, even planting trees will not be sufficient in removing enough greenhouse gases from the atmosphere to reverse climate change. 

In conclusion, climate change is a problem that needs to be tackled together by everyone. It requires global cooperation and unison to cut or completely stop the burning of fossil fuels for electricity and the production of plastics. The consequences of climate change are already appearing throughout different regions around the world be it intense floods, droughts, or storms. These consequences will only intensify and continue to endanger human livelihood unless we reach a compromise with nature and stop exploiting resources.

Climate change, a non-reversable hole in our world. I believe that it is incredibly important to care about climate change. Firstly, climate change affects our agriculture. Next, temperatures are rising. Finally, natural disasters are only worsening because of climate change. If we don't do something now, we may not be able to live on our green planet much longer. 

Firstly, our agriculture system has drastically changed to adapt to the consequences of climate change. We see on a daily how crop growth is being negatively affected. Crops are taking longer to grow and are needing much more attention. Climate change has changed the soil, becoming more dry and having less nutrients. These crops need the nutrients in the soil to grow bigger and better, but we've seen a huge decline in soil nutrients recently. Since the crops are lacking in nutrients, we have to use chemicals to ensure that we can get food to eat, but are these crops as good as we think if they are grown with harmful chemicals? In the end it is us who suffers and it is us who need to take action on caring for our environment. 

Secondly, global temperatures are rising putting humans and many animals in danger. Many scientists have been talking about the global temperature and how it is rising. Even if the temperature is slightly rising, it is still rising and causing much harm. Rising temperatures cause drought, glaciers to melt and an increase in wildfires. All of these together cause harm to humans and animals. With warmer temperatures, animals used to the cold will have to suffer, as they aren't used to hot temperatures and need the cold to survive. Humans will also be affected as droughts affect our crop growth and wildfires are ruining our clean air. It is crucial that we start caring for our environment after realizing the harm in rising temperatures. 

Lastly, climate change is increasing natural disasters. The warmer temperatures are causing more fires to happen, especially large wildfires. Not too long ago was Ontario, Quebec and parts of the United States  being heavily affected due to the wildfires accross Quebec. Our skies were red, it was harder to breathe and quite difficult to see through the smoke. We are seeing the huge increase in wildfires and we are suffering through the consequences. We are also seeing more natural disasters like earthquakes and tsunamis, that are linked to climate change. We must create change in our care for climate change. 

In conclusion, it is necesary that we start to make a bigger effort to care about climate change to save our planet. Climate change is affecting agriculture, it is contributing to rising temperatures and we are seeing an incline in natural disasters. If we don't start to care about climate change, we won't be able to have a healthy and safe life on Earth.

A common concern that parents have towards their teenagers being burnt-out comes from them being overloaded with work. This, however, does not arise from them being too "busy" or pressured but rather them lacking the ability to track their time. Furthermore, I believe that social media plays another critical role in creating this illusion of being "too busy". Recent studies show that teenagers are on their phones for an average of 3+ hours a day! That is a lot of valuable time that can be better spent elsewhere, such as finishing needed tasks. On top of the major time consumption, social media also affects the teenager's brain and cognitive abilities. By releasing heavy amounts of dopamine into their brain, it makes everything else seem less pleasurable to do, leading to procrastination. This effect makes it extremely difficult for teenagers to start other activities that don't involve being on the phone which ultimately, leads to more and more uncompleted tasks pilling up on them. Overall, I believe that social media and its intoxicating effects is one of the main reasons why teenagers feel as though they are over-pressured and unmotivated.

All in all, I believe that the misconception of teenagers being too busy comes down to their life habits. Someone with a social media addiction or poor time management skills is going to feel extremely overwhelmed over even the tiniest quantity of work. Establishing a sturdy schedule and social media regime is a great way for teenagers to avoid feeling over-pressured by work.

task_prompt: Would you live in a place that is always warm?
response_text:
Green grass, blue skies, blooming flowers, all things many love about the warm summer season, but what if it was all year round? A place where it was forever sunny and the cold of winter was unheard of. I would not live in a place that is always warm because of the heat, the bugs and the lack of other seasons.

     To begin, the heat and sun in warmer places can be unbearable. In order to be comfortable, one must constantly wear light clothing, both outdoors and indoors. Sometimes, even the smallest amount of clothing is not enough to stay cool. This would mean wearing small and uncomfortable clothing while remaining very hot. Moreover, the increased sun exposure that causes the heat will also cause sunburns. The solution to the issue is to constantly apply sunscreen, but forgetting for even one day can bring painful sunburns. The clothing required to wear for hot weather and sunburns are why I am not willing to live where it is always hot.

     Secondly, due to the constant warmth, bugs will be present year-round. While upon first impression bugs do not seem to pose much of an issue, they can be very dangerous. For example, mosquitoes are notorious for leaving bites on people that can cause itching for days on end. Not only that, but mosquitoes can also spread diseases that can be life-threatening. Having to always worry about bites from insects is an anxiety that comes with living in a hot place. In addition, many people, such as myself, are afraid of bugs. Living in a  warm climate would mean to be subjected to that fear on a regular basis as they are unavoidable. Bug bites and a fear of bugs is why living with many insects is difficult.

     Lastly, living in a warm place would mean that there is little to no variety in season. First, in such a place, the autumn and winter, two beautiful seasons, seasons would not be experienced. In a warm place, the change of seasons will not occur and the weather will not change much, it will stay the same : boring and hot. Additionally, the weather during holidays will not be what is expected. For holidays such as Halloween and Christmas, there is a certain change of weather that is expected and encourages the festive mood. Without this change, the holidays do not evoke the same feelings and are therefore less enjoyable. Missing the cold seasons and holidays is why somewhere with a lack of seasons is not great to live in.

     In conclusion, I would not live in a hot place because of its warmth, the insects and the missing variety of seasons. If anything, I would much rather live in a place that is always cold. Unfortunately, the Earths temperature is rising at an alarming rate, making many areas around the world too hot and, eventually, unlivable. If society fails to slow this down, future generations may not experience seasons and many other aspects of nature as we do today.
